item.title: A Practical Protocol for Quantum Oblivious Transfer from One-Way Functions
item.description:
Overview

This article presents a simulation-secure quantum oblivious-transfer protocol from one-way functions in the plain model, with explicit attention to efficiency, experimental errors, and the required quantum resources.

Publication details

  • Journal: Quantum
  • Volume and article: Volume 10, article 2124
  • Published: 1 June 2026
  • DOI: 10.22331/q-2026-06-01-2124
  • Preprint: arXiv:2406.09110, version 4 of 29 May 2026

Citation

Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, and Álvaro Yángüez, “A Practical Protocol for Quantum Oblivious Transfer from One-Way Functions,” Quantum 10, 2124 (2026). Download the BibTeX entry.

item.title: Efficient Quantum Measurements: Computational Max- and Measured Rényi Divergences and Applications
item.description:
Overview

This article introduces computational max-divergence and computational measured Rényi divergences constrained by efficient binary measurements, and develops applications to hypothesis testing and quantum resource quantification.

Publication details

  • Journal: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
  • Issue: Volume 72, issue 6
  • Pages: 4085–4114
  • Published: June 2026; first published online 2 April 2026
  • DOI: 10.1109/TIT.2026.3680247
  • Preprint: arXiv:2509.21308

Citation

Álvaro Yángüez, Thomas A. Hahn, and Jan Kochanowski, “Efficient Quantum Measurements: Computational Max- and Measured Rényi Divergences and Applications,” IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 72(6), 4085–4114 (2026). Download the BibTeX entry.

item.title: Accessible Quantum Correlations Under Complexity Constraints
item.description:
Overview

This preprint studies bipartite quantum states through efficiently implementable quantum channels, leading to computational versions of max-divergence and conditional min-entropy.

Publication details

  • Status: Preprint
  • Submitted: 16 April 2026
  • Identifier: arXiv:2604.15540 [quant-ph]
  • Subjects: Quantum Physics; Computational Complexity; Information Theory

Citation

Álvaro Yángüez, Noam Avidan, Jan Kochanowski, and Thomas A. Hahn, “Accessible Quantum Correlations Under Complexity Constraints,” arXiv:2604.15540 (2026). Download the BibTeX entry.

item.title: Quantum pseudoresources imply cryptography
item.description:
Overview

This article shows that quantum pseudoresources imply EPFI pairs and that EPFI pairs are equivalent to quantum commitments and therefore to EFI pairs, with a detailed treatment of pseudoentanglement.

Publication details

  • Journal: IACR Communications in Cryptology
  • Issue: Volume 2, issue 4
  • Length: 24 pages
  • Published: 8 January 2026
  • DOI: 10.62056/ahbngyl7s
  • Preprints: arXiv:2504.15025; IACR ePrint 2025/732

Citation

Alex B. Grilo and Álvaro Yángüez, “Quantum pseudoresources imply cryptography,” IACR Communications in Cryptology 2(4) (2026). Download the BibTeX entry.
